description.fun: Its body is a special metal, light and scratch-resistant, with a finish like a polished mirror, which makes it surprisingly agile. The only drawback is that it rusts easily, so Duraludon hates rain and lives in caves. Its rivalry with Tyranitar in Galar's mountains may nod to kaiju films, and its shape seems to be based on The Shard, the UK's tallest building.
description.guide: A Steel and Dragon-type Pokémon made of a light, strong metal that rusts easily. Duraludon has a Gigantamax form, and since The Indigo Disk it can evolve into Archaludon with a Metal Alloy.
description.tagline: A skyscraper-shaped dragon that hates the rain

description.fun: Grows into a full skyscraper, with a glass plate on its belly and window panels that glow with surplus energy. Its cells are exceptionally hard even for a Steel type, and its body is built to withstand earthquakes.

When danger comes, Archaludon drops onto all fours, straightens out and turns itself into a steel bridge. In that pose it fires tremendously powerful beams using static electricity gathered from the air, faster still in stormy weather. It's so durable that being caught in a cave-in won't faze it. Its legs and cables seem to borrow from Iberian bridges like the Guadiana International Bridge.
description.guide: The evolution of Duraludon, introduced in The Indigo Disk. A Steel and Dragon-type Pokémon based on cable-stayed bridges, it braces itself like a bridge to fire electric beams.
description.tagline: A dragon that turns itself into a steel bridge

note.text: Duraludon couldn't evolve at all until The Indigo Disk added Archaludon, making it the only Pokémon that could Gigantamax before it could evolve. Gigantamax belongs to Sword and Shield and Archaludon to Scarlet and Violet, so the two never appear in the same game.
